title: Wilson's 'Jess Express' campaign bus crashes into small business after just two hours on the road
text: Wilson’s ‘Jess Express’ campaign bus crashes into small business after just two hours on the road The bus ran into trouble on its first day on the road, damaging the awning of a jeweller in Melbourne’s south-east. The Victorian Liberal Party has had some early trouble on the first day aboard its campaign bus, which reversed into the awning of a small business and damaged the exterior. Opposition Leader Jess Wilson on Friday morning welcomed the press pack onto the Liberal’s big blue campaign bus – dubbed the Jess Express – and took to the streets of Bentleigh, in Melbourne’s south-east. But as the bus reversed into a park in the main shopping strip it hit with the awning of a local jeweller, peeling metal off the outside and making a loud scraping noise, as the media aboard cringed.It was an awkward moment and took media attention away from a planned photo op. But Wilson took it in her stride, continuing to campaign in the street and mix with local traders. The Liberals promised the repair costs would be covered, and a member of Wilson’s staff has been in contact with the business owner, who the campaign says was very understanding.It was rather ironic the bus damaged a small business, given Wilson was earlier slinging coffees at the Double Pour cafe and spruiking the Coalition’s promise to help local businesses by cutting land tax and payroll tax. ”. On each seat inside the bus was also an aeroplane-style passenger safety card offering a satirical “guide to surviving 12 years of Labor”. Labor swiftly unveiled its own, retaliatory safety cards for passengers on the Jess Express.”; beware erratic driving as “One Nation are in the driver’s seat”; and not to expect assistance in the event of a crash because “Liberals cut emergency services”. In 2017, Pauline Hanson’s “Battler Bus” broke down outside Rockhampton, Queensland, with a broken hose causing a three-hour delay. In what retrospectively might have been bad omens, both Bill Shorten and Peter Dutton received some unwanted publicity for bus bungles.Last year Dutton’s bus struck a concrete bike lane in Melbourne’s CBD, temporarily derailing the campaign. Bill Shorten’s team straighten a give way sign after it was struck by the Labor campaign bus in 2016. In 2016, the “Bill Bus” swiped a give way sign while campaigning in suburban Melbourne.
